rationale: Evidence from iteration 9 (base_speed 1.1, y 0.065, kd 0.6, kp 2.6, score 425.1 against 431.1 at 1.2). Oval finished 20/20 again, with mean score 951 (up from 944) and line_loss_events down to 0.15 (from 0.65). The s-bend still ended 20/20 off track, with max_error 0.0626 (at or above the 0.06 limit) and progress 0.57 (down from 0.63). Slalom still ended 20/20 off track with max_error 0.0655 and 1.0 line-loss events. Lowering speed therefore did not clear the s-bend, so speed is not the limiting factor. The approved feedback's rule applies: return base_speed to 1.2 and test kd 0.5 at y 0.065. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.1 to 1.2, which restores the iteration 8 speed. (2) kd 0.6 to 0.5. Less derivative damping may reduce the lag-driven overshoot on the s-bend, and slalom oscillation was 0.22 at kd 0.6, so a slightly softer derivative term may also help there. Everything else is held at iteration 8: x -0.07 to 0.07, y 0.065, sensor_size 0.016, kp 2.6, ki 0.1, line_loss last_direction, sensor_weights -2,-1,0,1,2, and the body, wheel and mass values. I am keeping y 0.065 despite the line-loss rise, since the approved feedback accepts that cost while the oval is at 20/20. Expected result: the oval stays at 20/20 with mean near 944, and s-bend max_error falls toward or below 0.06, with some s-bend finishes possible. Risk: kd 0.5 may raise oscillation on the oval and slalom, since iteration 4 at kd 0.45 showed weaker damping than iteration 5 at kd 0.6. Hypotheses to check: (a) s-bend max_error below 0.06 and s-bend finishes appear; (b) oval finishes stay at 17/20 or better; (c) slalom steering_oscillation stays near 0.22 or lower. If kd 0.5 worsens the oval or slalom without an s-bend gain, return kd to 0.6 and test base_speed 1.15 at y 0.065, or return y to 0.05 if line-loss events on the oval stay above about 0.3.
